issue.title: [cfggen] dict.keys()[0] raises TypeError in Python 3 (minigraph PEER_SWITCH warning)

failure.body:
### Description

`minigraph.py:2191` uses `results['PEER_SWITCH'].keys()[0]` which is invalid in Python 3. `dict.keys()` returns a view object, not a list, so indexing with `[0]` raises `TypeError`.

### Current code
```python
print("Warning: more than one peer switch was found. Only the first will be parsed: {}".format(
    results['PEER_SWITCH'].keys()[0]))  # TypeError in Python 3
```

Note that 2 lines below, the code correctly uses `list(results['PEER_SWITCH'].keys())[0]`.

### Fix
```python
next(iter(results['PEER_SWITCH']))
```

### Impact
Crashes `sonic-cfggen` when parsing a minigraph with more than one peer switch (DualToR configurations).

resolution.title: [agent][cfggen] Fix dict.keys()[0] TypeError in Python 3 for PEER_SWITCH warning
resolution.description:
#### What I did
Fix `results['PEER_SWITCH'].keys()[0]` which raises `TypeError` in Python 3 since `dict.keys()` returns a view, not a list.

#### How I did it
Replaced `results['PEER_SWITCH'].keys()[0]` with `next(iter(results['PEER_SWITCH']))`.

Note: the very next line (2193) already uses the correct `list(results['PEER_SWITCH'].keys())[0]` pattern.

#### How to verify it
Parse a minigraph with more than one peer switch (DualToR config).

#### Which release branch to backport
master

#### Description for the changelog
Fix Python 3 TypeError in minigraph PEER_SWITCH warning message.

Fixes: #26400
